title: These New Bose Over-the-Ear Headphones Are Made for Getting Lost in Music & Are Worth the Money
summary: With TrueSpatial technology, Immersion and Cinema modes, plus improved noise cancellation, Bose’s latest QuietComfort headphones pack in more flagship features.
contentText:

If there’s one headphone brand that has consistently earned its place among the biggest names in audio, it’s Bose . The brand’s QuietComfort line has become especially well known for its combination of comfortable over-ear designs, strong noise cancellation and reliable sound. In fact, my first pair of high-tech headphones was the first-generation QuietComfort model , which lasted more than six years of near-daily use.

That kind of longevity is a big reason Bose remains a go-to recommendation for headphones that are worth the investment. Now, the brand is building on that formula with the new Bose QuietComfort Headphones (2nd Gen), which are available to purchase from Bose , Amazon and other retailers.

Buy Bose QuietComfort Headphones (2nd gen)

Priced at $359, the over-ear headphones add more immersive audio, improved noise cancellation and a refreshed design while keeping some of the features that made the original QuietComfort headphones so popular.

Available colorways as of the time of this writing: Eucalyptus Green, Dewdrop Mint, Rosewood Mauve, White Smoke and Black.

The biggest upgrade is the addition of Bose’s TrueSpatial Technology, which is designed to make music and video feel more immersive by creating a wider, fuller soundstage. There are also two listening modes to play around with: Immersive Audio for music and video, and Cinema Mode, which spatializes compatible content while keeping dialogue centered.

Here’s What Else to Know About the Bose QuietComfort Headphones (2nd Gen):

- Noise cancellation: QuietControl noise cancellation with updated ActiveSense Technology that adjusts noise cancellation in Aware Mode

- Immersive audio: TrueSpatial Technology, Immersive Audio and Cinema Mode

- Microphones: Six microphones for clearer calls and improved noise cancellation

- Battery life: Up to 24 hours of playback, or up to 18 hours with Immersive Audio

- Quick charge: A 15-minute charge provides up to 2.5 hours of playback

- Connectivity: Bluetooth 5.4 with multipoint connectivity for two devices at once

- Wired listening: USB-C audio supports lossless input up to 24-bit/48 kHz and the box includes a USB-C-to-3.5mm cable

- Design: Pill-shaped earcups, a wider sliding headband, physical buttons and plush around-ear cushions

- Customization: Bose app lets you adjust settings and listening preferences

I’ve been lucky enough to test some of Bose’s other headphones along with its portable and waterproof speakers, and the brand has consistently impressed me with how much technology it packs into its products. But there’s something especially telling about a pair of headphones lasting more than six years while being used constantly, from blasting Charli xcx on my commute to getting lost in Tame Impala during late-night work sessions.

For me, that’s what makes the new QuietComfort Headphones (2nd Gen) worth paying attention to. Bose is adding newer technology without losing what made me love its headphones in the first place: comfortable listening, strong noise cancellation and sound that makes you want to stay in your music a little longer.
